title: Pad Krapao
subtitle: Thai basil stir-fry with chicken, garlic and chilli
excerpt: Pad krapao is one of Thailand's most popular street food dishes. Minced chicken is stir-fried over high heat with garlic, chilli, oyster sauce, and holy basil. Thai basil gives a slightly anise-flavoured freshness that wilts beautifully into the hot wok.
sourceNotes: Pad krapao (krapao means holy basil in Thai) is a national dish of Thailand often eaten for breakfast or lunch. It is cooked in a very hot wok in under 10 minutes and typically served over rice with a fried egg.

content.text: The wok must be very hot before you add anything. If the oil does not shimmer immediately when it goes in, wait longer. High heat is what gives this dish its characteristic slightly smoky wok flavour.

items.prepNote: minced in a food processor or bought minced
finely sliced, seeds in for more heat

content.text: Mix the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl and set aside.
Heat the wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add the oil.
Add the garlic and chilli. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken mince. Break it up with a spatula. Stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through and beginning to crisp in places.
Pour in the sauce. Toss everything together for 1 minute.
Take the wok off the heat. Add the Thai basil and toss. The basil will wilt in the residual heat.
Serve over jasmine rice with a fried egg on top.

items.symptom: Chicken is steaming and not getting any colour.
items.cause: Wok was not hot enough or chicken was too wet.
items.fix: Blast wok heat higher; cook in two batches if wok is small.

items.cause: Soy sauce and fish sauce are both strong.
items.fix: Add a squeeze of lime and a little more honey to balance.
